newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks firmer at opening, aided by bonds.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks firmer at opening, aided by bonds.

text.p: The Australian share market firmed at the opening on Wednesday, encouraged by a stronger bond market after the U.S. Fed left U.S. interest rates unchanged and by firmer base metals prices.
The All Ordinaries index was 8.8 points higher at 2237.5 in early trading.
With bonds responding positively to developments in the U.S., brokers said investor interest was mainly on the buy side.
"There is not a lot of interest but what there is seems to be on the buy side," said a Sydney broker.
Buying was concentrated on resource leaders BHP and CRA and in the banking sector.
"CRA and BHP are both better in the resources, the banks are better as well and that is helping things along," the broker said.
BHP was up 18 cents at A$16.10 while CRA was up 20 at A$18.32. Commonwealth Bank instalment receipts were up 18 cents at A$7.25 to stand out in the banking sector.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about five to two, while about 41 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
